quests.instruction: What is a family tradition?
quests.correctAnswer: Something a family repeats and passes on 🔁
options: Something a family repeats and passes on 🔁
Something a family does once and forgets 🕰️
A rule that only the adults must follow 📏
quests.hint: Think about something your family does every year or every week.
quests.explanation: A tradition is something a family does again and again over time, and it is often handed down from older people to younger ones.
quests.funFact: The word 'tradition' comes from a Latin word meaning 'to hand over'.

quests.instruction: Every year when the first rains come, Ekow's family makes hot snacks and sits on the porch to watch. What is this?
quests.correctAnswer: A family tradition 🌧️
options: A sudden accident 💥
A school homework task 📚
A family tradition 🌧️
quests.hint: It is repeated each year, and the family looks forward to it.
quests.explanation: Doing the same special thing each year, and looking forward to it, makes it a tradition. Traditions can be small and personal.
quests.funFact: Many families have small traditions tied to the weather or seasons, like the first snow or the first mango.

quests.instruction: Which of these can be a family tradition?
quests.correctAnswer: A bedtime song or Friday pizza night 🍕
options: Only big festivals with many guests 🎉
Only things that cost a lot of money 💰
A bedtime song or Friday pizza night 🍕
quests.hint: Traditions can be big or small.
quests.explanation: Traditions do not need to be fancy. Small things done together, like a song or a weekly meal, can mean a lot.
quests.funFact: Researchers who study families say that small, regular rituals often matter as much as big celebrations.

quests.instruction: Femi's family wants to start a new tradition. Which idea is the best start?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask everyone and choose together 🗣️
options: Decide alone and tell others to follow 📢
Ask everyone and choose together 🗣️
Copy another family's tradition exactly 📋
quests.hint: Traditions work best when people enjoy them.
quests.explanation: A tradition feels special when everyone has a say, so asking for ideas helps it fit the whole family.
quests.funFact: Some families start traditions as simple as a weekly walk or a yearly photo in the same spot.

quests.instruction: Gabi's family moves to a new country and cannot find all the ingredients for their holiday meal. What is a good idea?
quests.correctAnswer: Adapt it with what they can find 🍲
options: Give up on the holiday for good 🚫
Pretend the holiday is not happening 🙈
Adapt it with what they can find 🍲
quests.hint: A tradition can bend without breaking.
quests.explanation: Traditions often change to suit new places and new circumstances. The meaning matters more than having every ingredient.
quests.funFact: Many dishes that people think of as 'traditional' have changed over the years as ingredients and places changed.

quests.instruction: A birthday tradition in Hanne's family is to tease the birthday person, and her cousin gets upset. What could the family do?
quests.correctAnswer: Adjust it so everyone feels good 💛
options: Tell the cousin to stop being upset 🙄
Adjust it so everyone feels good 💛
Keep teasing even more loudly 😆
quests.hint: A good tradition makes people feel included.
quests.explanation: Traditions are meant to bring people closer. If one hurts someone's feelings, the family can change it.
quests.funFact: Families can keep the parts of a tradition that they love and change the parts that do not work.

quests.instruction: Why do families celebrate special days?
quests.correctAnswer: To mark something special together 🎉
options: To spend as much money as possible 💸
To keep everyone apart for the day 🚪
To mark something special together 🎉
quests.hint: Think about how you feel at a celebration.
quests.explanation: Celebrations mark important moments such as birthdays, harvests, or new seasons, and give people a chance to share joy and connect.
quests.funFact: Archaeologists have found evidence of feasts and celebrations from thousands of years ago.

quests.instruction: Onam is a festival celebrated by many families in Kerala. What is it mainly connected to?
quests.correctAnswer: The harvest season 🌾
options: A winter snowfall ❄️
The harvest season 🌾
A school exam season 📚
quests.hint: It comes at the end of the rains, when crops are gathered.
quests.explanation: Onam is a harvest festival in Kerala. It is celebrated with flower carpets called pookalam and a feast called the sadya.
quests.funFact: A traditional sadya has many dishes served on a banana leaf.

quests.instruction: Lunar New Year is celebrated by many families in different countries. What is the 'lunar' part about?
quests.correctAnswer: It follows the moon's cycles 🌙
options: It follows only the sun's position ☀️
It follows the moon's cycles 🌙
It always falls on January 1 📅
quests.hint: 'Lunar' is a word about the moon.
quests.explanation: Lunar New Year dates come from a calendar based on the moon, so the date changes from year to year.
quests.funFact: Lunar New Year can fall anywhere from late January to mid-February.

quests.instruction: Families around the world eat different staple foods, such as rice, flatbread, tortillas, or potatoes. What does this show?
quests.correctAnswer: Many different foods nourish families 🍽️
options: Only one kind of food is correct 🏆
Some families choose the wrong food 🙅
Many different foods nourish families 🍽️
quests.hint: Think about what feeds people in different places.
quests.explanation: Different places grow and cook different foods. All kinds of foods can feed a family well.
quests.funFact: Rice is a main food for more than half of the world's people.

quests.instruction: At a friend's home, Soren notices that the family eats with their hands. What is a respectful thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Watch and ask how it is done 👀
options: Say that it looks gross to him 🤢
Refuse to eat anything at all 🚫
Watch and ask how it is done 👀
quests.hint: Be curious, not critical.
quests.explanation: In many places, people eat with their hands, chopsticks, spoons, or forks. Watching and asking politely shows respect.
quests.funFact: Eating with the hands is common in many parts of the world, and many cultures have special etiquette for it.

quests.instruction: Rania's family sits on a floor mat to eat, and Soren's family sits at a table. Which statement is fair?
quests.correctAnswer: Both are fine ways to eat together 🍽️
options: Both are fine ways to eat together 🍽️
Only eating at a table is polite 🪑
Only eating on the floor is polite 🧶
quests.hint: Think about what matters at a shared meal: the people, not the furniture.
quests.explanation: Families eat in many ways, at tables, on mats, or on benches. What matters is sharing the meal.
quests.funFact: In some homes, meals are traditionally eaten seated on the floor.

quests.instruction: Tasha is visiting Kavi, whose family keeps phones away at dinner. What should Tasha do?
quests.correctAnswer: Follow the house's dinner rule 📵
options: Follow the house's dinner rule 📵
Say the rule is silly 🙄
Leave the table and use her phone 🚪
quests.hint: When you are a guest, you follow the house rules.
quests.explanation: Each household has its own habits. As a guest, following them is a way to show respect.
quests.funFact: Guests in many cultures are expected to follow the customs of their hosts.

quests.instruction: Some homes are quiet and some are very chatty. What is a fair thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: Both are normal ways to be 💛
options: Chatty homes are always rude 🔊
Quiet homes are always boring 🤫
Both are normal ways to be 💛
quests.hint: Think about what makes a home comfortable for the people in it.
quests.explanation: Households have different styles. Neither is better. What matters is that people feel comfortable and respected.
quests.funFact: People can feel at home in a lively kitchen or a quiet corner, depending on their style.

quests.instruction: Yaw smells a food he has never smelled at his friend's house. What is a polite thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: 'Interesting smell! What is it?' 🙂
options: 'Ew, what is that horrible smell?' 😖
'I am not going to eat that at all.' 🚫
'Interesting smell! What is it?' 🙂
quests.hint: Show curiosity, not disgust.
quests.explanation: Polite curiosity lets you learn about a new food without hurting anyone's feelings.
quests.funFact: The sense of smell is closely linked to memory, so a smell can remind people of home.

quests.instruction: Zuri's family has a recipe handed down from her great-grandmother. Why is it special?
quests.correctAnswer: It connects generations of the family 🍲
options: Because it costs a lot of money 💰
It connects generations of the family 🍲
Because nobody is allowed to eat it 🚫
quests.hint: Think about who cooked it before.
quests.explanation: A recipe that has been passed down connects people with their ancestors and shares family history in every meal.
quests.funFact: Many families keep handwritten recipe cards with notes in the cook's own handwriting.

quests.instruction: Which is a good way to keep family stories alive?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask elders and record their stories 🎤
options: Ask elders and record their stories 🎤
Never mention the past to anyone 🤐
Throw away old photos and letters 🗑️
quests.hint: Stories live on when someone listens and keeps them.
quests.explanation: Asking older relatives for stories, and writing or recording them, helps keep memories for the next generations.
quests.funFact: Some people record family stories on a phone so they can listen to them years later.

quests.instruction: Jiro's grandfather gives him an old watch that has been in the family for years. How should Jiro treat it?
quests.correctAnswer: Look after it carefully 🕰️
options: Look after it carefully 🕰️
Use it as a toy at the park 🛝
Leave it somewhere forgotten 🗑️
quests.hint: Objects that carry family history deserve care.
quests.explanation: Family heirlooms carry memories. Handling them gently and storing them safely keeps them for the future.
quests.funFact: An object that is passed down in a family is called an heirloom.

quests.instruction: Which of these is a weekly family routine, not a special yearly celebration?
quests.correctAnswer: A Sunday call with Grandma 📞
options: The big feast once a year 🎉
A birthday party for a cousin 🎂
A Sunday call with Grandma 📞
quests.hint: A weekly routine happens every week.
quests.explanation: Routines repeat often and keep the family connected. Special celebrations happen on certain days.
quests.funFact: Many families find that regular calls help relatives who live far away stay close.

quests.instruction: Why do families need both routines and special days?
quests.correctAnswer: Routines steady us; parties lift us 🌈
options: Routines steady us; parties lift us 🌈
Routines are boring, so skip them all 😴
Special days replace every routine 🔄
quests.hint: Think about what each one gives a family.
quests.explanation: Routines make life feel steady and predictable, and celebrations add joy and memories. Families usually enjoy both.
quests.funFact: Children tend to feel more secure when daily life has a steady rhythm.

quests.instruction: Ciro's grandmother lives somewhere that is 3 hours behind his time. If it is 7:00 pm for Ciro, what time is it for her?
quests.hint: Behind means earlier on the clock.
quests.explanation: If her time is 3 hours behind, subtract 3 hours: 7:00 pm minus 3 hours is 4:00 pm.
quests.funFact: The world is divided into time zones, so it can be morning in one country and evening in another at the same moment.

quests.instruction: Dalila invites friends to a party, and one friend does not eat meat. What is a thoughtful plan?
quests.correctAnswer: Make sure there is a meat-free dish 🥗
options: Serve only meat dishes and say nothing 🍖
Make sure there is a meat-free dish 🥗
Ask the friend to bring all their own food 🚪
quests.hint: A good host plans for guests' needs.
quests.explanation: Some people do not eat meat for health, belief, or choice. A good host makes sure everyone has something to eat.
quests.funFact: Many cuisines around the world have long traditions of delicious meat-free dishes.

quests.instruction: Before a gathering, what is a good way to find out what guests can eat?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask them kindly beforehand 💬
options: Ask them kindly beforehand 💬
Guess based on where they come from 🌍
Assume everyone eats everything 🍽️
quests.hint: Do not assume. Ask.
quests.explanation: People's food needs depend on health, beliefs, allergies, and tastes, not on the country their family is from. Asking is respectful and avoids stereotypes.
quests.funFact: Food allergies and food rules vary a lot from person to person, so asking is the safest way to be sure.

quests.instruction: Oleg offers a popular dish to a new friend whose family is from a country where many people eat it. His friend says his family does not eat it. What did Oleg learn?
quests.correctAnswer: Not every family follows the same custom 💛
options: His friend is wrong about his own family 🙅
Not every family follows the same custom 💛
All families from a country eat the same 🍽️
quests.hint: People in the same country can live very differently.
quests.explanation: Families within any country or culture differ a lot. Assuming everyone is the same is a stereotype. Asking is better.
quests.funFact: Even within one family, people can have different tastes and habits.

quests.instruction: Grandma used to host the big family meal, but now it is too tiring for her. How can the tradition continue?
quests.correctAnswer: Everyone shares the cooking 🤝
options: Everyone shares the cooking 🤝
End the tradition for good 🚫
Ask Grandma to cook it all alone 👵
quests.hint: A tradition can change who does the work.
quests.explanation: Traditions can continue in new ways. Sharing the work keeps the tradition and respects Grandma's energy.
quests.funFact: Many family gatherings use a potluck, where each person brings one dish.

quests.instruction: Viktor's mom marries someone whose family has a different holiday custom. What is a good way to bring the families together?
quests.correctAnswer: Share both and blend them 🤝
options: Share both and blend them 🤝
Keep only the oldest family's custom 🏆
Cancel the holiday so nobody argues 🚫
quests.hint: Think about honoring both families.
quests.explanation: In blended families, mixing customs lets everyone feel included and can create new traditions.
quests.funFact: Many families create new 'fusion' traditions when they combine different customs.

quests.instruction: Xiu's family always has a big party on her birthday, but she prefers a quiet day. What can she do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell her family what she would enjoy 💬
options: Say nothing and feel unhappy all day 😶
Tell her family what she would enjoy 💬
Cancel her birthday without telling anyone 🚫
quests.hint: Share your wishes kindly.
quests.explanation: Traditions are for the whole family, including Xiu. Telling them what she would enjoy helps find something everyone likes.
quests.funFact: Many families make small changes to traditions to suit different people.

quests.instruction: Which sentence about traditions is true?
quests.correctAnswer: They can be small, big, and can change 🔁
options: They must stay exactly the same forever 🔒
They can be small, big, and can change 🔁
Only some kinds of families may have them 🚫
quests.hint: Think about everything you have learned in this level.
quests.explanation: Traditions can be big or small, and they can grow and change as families do. Every family can have them.
quests.funFact: Some traditions are thousands of years old, and others are invented this year.

quests.instruction: At a friend's home, the family says a short thank-you before eating, which you do not do at home. What is the best response?
quests.correctAnswer: Wait quietly and respect their custom 🙏
options: Laugh and ask why they are so weird 😆
Start eating before everyone else 🍽️
Wait quietly and respect their custom 🙏
quests.hint: Respect your hosts' way of doing things.
quests.explanation: Waiting respectfully shows respect for a family's customs. You can ask about it afterwards if you are curious.
quests.funFact: Many cultures have a short moment of thanks or blessing before meals.

quests.instruction: Two families are planning a joint celebration. One wants a loud party and the other wants a quiet meal. Which plan respects both?
quests.correctAnswer: A quiet meal, then music and games 🎶
options: Do only what the loud family likes 📢
A quiet meal, then music and games 🎶
Do only what the quiet family likes 🤫
quests.hint: Look for a plan that gives something to each family.
quests.explanation: A compromise that includes both ideas, such as a quiet meal followed by music, respects both families.
quests.funFact: Many celebrations around the world include both a shared meal and music or dance.
